bibl.title: Large-scale recording of neurons by movable silicon probes in behaving rodents

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: The construction and implantation of a movable silicon-probe microdrive for chronic recording in freely moving rodents.
span.quote: Here, we describe methods for recording multiple single neurons and local field potential in behaving rodents, using commercially available micro-machined silicon probes with custom-made accessory components.

span.label: method
span.quote: Here, we describe methods for recording multiple single neurons and local field potential in behaving rodents, using commercially available micro-machined silicon probes with custom-made accessory components.

span.label: chronic large-scale silicon-probe recording in behaving rodents
span.quote: This movie illustrates the implantation procedure of silicon probes for chronic large-scale recordings in the behaving rat.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: Each step of the probe preparation, microdrive construction and surgery is illustrated so that the end user can easily replicate the process.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Any break in the ground path (CSF to ground screw to copper wire to copper mesh to ground pin) leaves the headstage ungrounded, which is why movement artifacts and 50/60 Hz line noise appear in the recording
span.quote: the electrical path of the grounding should be checked, as any circuit interruption between the cerebrospinal fluid, the ground screw, the copper wire, the copper mesh flaps and the ground pin on the connector, would result in a large movement artifacts and/or line noise (50 Hz or 60 Hz).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A micro-drive protruding above a too-short Faraday cage picks up environmental electrical fields, acting as an antenna and injecting noise into the signal
span.quote: If the Faraday cage is not high enough, the protruding micro-drive may act as an antenna.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The copper-mesh cylinder encloses the headgear and shunts environmental fields and whisker-generated charge to ground, which is how it suppresses noise and slow-wave artifacts
span.quote: The cylinder also serves as an electrical shield against environmental noise and the slow wave artifacts produced by the charged whiskers in the behaving animal.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Placing the reference over the cerebellum exploits the fact that cerebellar LFP amplitude and midline muscle artifact are both minimal, so the referenced signal carries less contamination
span.quote: This site is chosen because cerebellar LFP is the smallest of all cortical regions and muscle artifacts are minimal at this midline location.

span.label: The microdrive design is a set of trade-offs rather than an optimum, which is why different drives suit different applications
span.quote: As a result of these competing requirements, different drives suite different applications.

span.label: The probe shanks must be aligned parallel to the travel axis so that advancing moves them through tissue rather than cutting across it
span.quote: This ensures that during advancement, the probe shanks move into brain tissue without 'cutting' through it.

span.label: Insulation at the bonding area keeps cerebrospinal fluid from short-circuiting the connections
span.quote: Before fixing the probe to the drive, add extra insulation to the bonding area of the probe to prevent cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) or humidity from producing short-circuits:

span.label: Grounding is a continuous electrical path through fluid, screw, wire and mesh, and a break anywhere in it produces artefact or mains noise
span.quote: In addition, the electrical path of the grounding should be checked, as any circuit interruption between the cerebrospinal fluid, the ground screw, the copper wire, the copper mesh flaps and the ground pin on the connector, would result in a large movement artifacts and/or line noise (50 Hz or 60 Hz).

span.label: A protruding drive above the shielding acts as an antenna, which is fixed by grounding the drive itself
span.quote: The antenna effect can be prevented by grounding the drive as well (solder another copper wire between the drive and the copper-mesh).

span.label: Recording alone cannot settle cause and effect, so the remedy is to identify cell types and then drive them - which is where optogenetics enters
span.quote: The efficient combination large scale recordings and optical methods with silicon probes 23 provides the means for both identifying and selectively driving specific cell populations, therefore allowing to address the causal relationships in brain networks.

span.label: The measurements are correlational, so causal relations among neuronal activity patterns cannot be resolved by this method.
span.note: what this limits: any cause-effect reading of the recordings the method produces: GIVEN THE CORRELATIONAL NATURE OF THESE MEASUREMENTS, THE CAUSE-EFFECT RELATIONSHIP ... REMAINS INEVITABLY AMBIGUOUS
span.quote: However, given the correlational nature of these measurements, the cause-effect relationship among neuronal activity patterns remains inevitably ambiguous.

span.label: Only a single-probe implantation is demonstrated; multi-probe recording is asserted but not shown.
span.note: what this limits: the multi-probe claim: WE ILLUSTRATED THE IMPLANTATION OF A SINGLE SILICON PROBE, and the rest CAN BE READILY ACCOMPLISHED AFTER SOME PRACTICE - asserted, not demonstrated
span.quote: We illustrated the implantation of a single silicon probe, but multiple site recordings using multiple probes and drives can be readily accomplished after some practice.

span.label: The filmed surgery is a demonstration in which several preparatory, surgical and postoperative steps are omitted.
span.note: what this limits: the video as a protocol to work from: SEVERAL PREPARATORY STEPS, SURGICAL PRECAUTIONS AND POSTOPERATIVE PROCEDURES ARE NOT SHOWN/VISIBLE OR DISCUSSED
span.quote: For appropriate visibility and filming purposes, several preparatory steps, surgical precautions and postoperative procedures are not shown/visible or discussed.

span.label: The authors state the correlational limit of the whole method: no amount of recording settles cause and effect
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - no quantity of recording settles cause and effect
span.quote: However, given the correlational nature of these measurements, the cause-effect relationship among neuronal activity patterns remains inevitably ambiguous.

span.label: Both the tissue and the probe are fragile, and the critical steps are the ones where either can be damaged
span.note: what this limits: the success rate: CRITICAL STEPS ... ARISE FROM THE FRAGILITY OF BOTH BIOLOGICAL (BRAIN TISSUE) AND TECHNICAL (SILICON PROBE) MATERIALS
span.quote: Critical steps to ensure quality recordings of neuronal activity arise from the fragility of both biological (brain tissue) and technical (silicon probe) materials.

span.label: Injury during preparation or afterwards destroys the unit activity the method exists to capture
span.note: what this limits: the unit activity the method exists to capture: ANY INJURY TO THE BRAIN TISSUE ... WOULD RESULT IN DAMAGING THE CELLS AND JEOPARDIZING THE RECORDING OF UNIT ACTIVITY
span.quote: Similarly, any injury to the brain tissue (while preparing the brain surface for implantation, or from bumping into the probe or drive once it is implanted) would result in damaging the cells and jeopardizing the recording of unit activity.

span.label: The filmed procedure omits preparatory, surgical and postoperative steps for the sake of visibility
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 2, stated outright: THE (MOCK) SURGERY SHOWN IN THIS VIDEO IS FOR DEMONSTRATION PURPOSES ONLY
span.quote: Please note that the (mock) surgery shown in this video is for demonstration purposes only.

span.label: Only a single-probe implantation is demonstrated, with multi-probe work left to practice
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 1 - one probe shown, multiple probes asserted
span.quote: We illustrated the implantation of a single silicon probe, but multiple site recordings using multiple probes and drives can be readily accomplished after some practice.

span.label: recording - as evidence about WHAT HAPPENS: which neurons fire when, which the method delivers at scale
span.quote: Understanding of input-output relationships of neurons and circuits requires methods with the spatial selectivity and temporal resolution appropriate for mechanistic analysis of neural ensembles in the behaving animal, i.e. recording of representatively large samples of isolated single neurons.

span.label: recording - as evidence about WHAT CAUSES WHAT: which it cannot deliver at any scale, because the measurements are correlational
span.quote: However, given the correlational nature of these measurements, the cause-effect relationship among neuronal activity patterns remains inevitably ambiguous.

span.label: the limit - as a matter of SAMPLE SIZE: solvable by recording more neurons, perhaps every neuron in the volume
span.quote: Recent theoretical and experimental studies with silicon probes 17,19 indicate that with properly refined large-scale recording methods, combined with new mathematical insights and modeling studies, one will be able to record from a representatively large fraction or perhaps every neuron from the brain volume surveyed by a multiple shank silicon probe (thousands of cells in ~1 μm 3;5-17 ).

span.label: the limit - as a matter of KIND: not solvable by more recording at all, and requiring identification plus manipulation instead
span.quote: A thorough understanding of how coordinated ensemble activity emerges from its neuronal components requires at least two additional steps.

span.label: claim_type: method
span.note: a second reading reaching the same value. Recorded: method — a second reading reaching the same value from a different sentence. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Each step of the probe preparation, microdrive construction and surgery is illustrated so that the end user can easily replicate the process.

span.label: phenomenon: chronic large-scale silicon-probe recording in behaving rodents
span.note: a second reading reaching the same value. Recorded: chronic large-scale silicon-probe recording in behaving rodents — a second reading reaching the same value from a different sentence. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: A major challenge in neuroscience is linking behavior to the collective activity of neural assemblies.

span.label: extends → the decade of ensemble recording work in small and large-brained animals including humans
span.quote: Ensemble monitoring of neuronal activity has progressed remarkably in the past decade in both small and large-brained animals, including human subjects 1-11 .

span.label: critiques → the sufficiency of recording alone for understanding circuit mechanism
span.quote: However, given the correlational nature of these measurements, the cause-effect relationship among neuronal activity patterns remains inevitably ambiguous.

span.label: silicon probes —operationalised-as→ unit activity
span.quote: Here, we describe methods for recording multiple single neurons and local field potential in behaving rodents, using commercially available micro-machined silicon probes with custom-made accessory components.

span.label: microdrive —part-of→ silicon probes
span.quote: Here, we describe the implantation of a 4-shank, 32-site probe attached to flexible polyimide cable, and mounted on a movable microdrive.

span.label: shank —part-of→ silicon probes
span.quote: Recent theoretical and experimental studies with silicon probes 17,19 indicate that with properly refined large-scale recording methods, combined with new mathematical insights and modeling studies, one will be able to record from a representatively large fraction or perhaps every neuron from the brain volume surveyed by a multiple shank silicon probe (thousands of cells in ~1 μm 3;5-17 ).

span.label: cluster analysis —operationalised-as→ unit activity
span.quote: To analyze neuronal unit activity, spikes are detected and sorted into single units using cluster analysis of their waveforms 15-16 .

span.label: theta —part-of→ local field potential
span.quote: Note the prominent 8 Hz (theta band) oscillation of the local field potential during exploration with superimposed spiking on multiple shanks and sites (examples of spikes indicated by arrowheads).

span.label: impedance —operationalised-as→ silicon probes
span.quote: Before fixing the probe to the drive, the impedance of each recording site should be checked:

span.label: correlational —contrasted-with→ optogenetic
span.quote: The recently developed molecular optogenetic tools can be used to manipulate specific cell populations by local light stimulation 20-22 .

span.label: cell types —part-of→ neural assemblies
span.quote: The first one is the identification of the multiple neuronal cell types, each of which uniquely contributes to assembly behavior - literally like members of an orchestra.

span.label: optogenetic —operationalised-as→ cell types
span.quote: The efficient combination large scale recordings and optical methods with silicon probes 23 provides the means for both identifying and selectively driving specific cell populations, therefore allowing to address the causal relationships in brain networks.

span.label: DiI —operationalised-as→ shank
span.quote: Optional: for visualizing the probe track in the brain, DiI solution (1-2% diluted in ethanol) can be applied to the back of the probe at this stage.

span.label: neural assemblies —part-of→ unit activity
span.quote: A major challenge in neuroscience is linking behavior to the collective activity of neural assemblies.

span.label: cluster analysis
span.quote: To analyze neuronal unit activity, spikes are detected and sorted into single units using cluster analysis of their waveforms

span.label: Commercially available silicon probes with flexible cables and small multichannel preamplifiers have made simultaneous recording from 64-128 sites in a behaving rodent as easy as recording from 2 wire-electrode sites a decade earlier.
span.quote: Today, it is as easy to record from 64 to 128 sites simultaneously in a behaving rodent as from 2 sites with wire electrodes just a decade ago.

span.label: Silicon-based multiple-site devices are effective for ensemble recording because they scale to many sites, occupy small volume, and have controlled geometric design.
span.quote: Multiple-site recording with silicon-based devices are particularly effective because of their scalability, small volume and geometric design.

span.label: In a rat exploring an open field, 32-channel CA1 recordings show a prominent 8 Hz theta oscillation in the local field potential with unit spikes superimposed across several shanks and recording sites.
span.quote: Note the prominent 8 Hz (theta band) oscillation of the local field potential during exploration with superimposed spiking on multiple shanks and sites

span.label: The recorded electrophysiological signals depend both on which brain structure the probe sits in and on what the animal is doing at the time.
span.quote: Electrophysiological signals (local field potential and unit activity) vary depending on the recorded structure and the current behavior of the animal.

span.label: Even large-scale silicon-probe recordings cannot establish cause and effect between neuronal activity patterns, because the measurements are purely correlational.
span.quote: However, given the correlational nature of these measurements, the cause-effect relationship among neuronal activity patterns remains inevitably ambiguous.

span.label: The authors project that refined large-scale probes combined with new mathematical and modelling work will allow recording from a representatively large fraction, or perhaps all, of the neurons in the volume a multi-shank probe surveys.
span.quote: Recent theoretical and experimental studies with silicon probes 17,19 indicate that with properly refined large-scale recording methods, combined with new mathematical insights and modeling studies, one will be able to record from a representatively large fraction or perhaps every neuron from the brain volume surveyed by a multiple shank silicon probe

span.label: recording from 64 to 128 sites in a behaving rodent is now as easy as two sites were a decade earlier
span.quote: Today, it is as easy to record from 64 to 128 sites simultaneously in a behaving rodent as from 2 sites with wire electrodes just a decade ago.

span.label: the example recordings show theta-band field oscillation with spiking superimposed across shanks during exploration
span.quote: Note the prominent 8 Hz (theta band) oscillation of the local field potential during exploration with superimposed spiking on multiple shanks and sites (examples of spikes indicated by arrowheads).

span.label: recording every neuron in the surveyed volume is projected as reachable, and would still not resolve causation
span.quote: Recent theoretical and experimental studies with silicon probes 17,19 indicate that with properly refined large-scale recording methods, combined with new mathematical insights and modeling studies, one will be able to record from a representatively large fraction or perhaps every neuron from the brain volume surveyed by a multiple shank silicon probe (thousands of cells in ~1 μm 3;5-17 ).

span.label: ideal microdrive
span.quote: An ideal microdrive allows smooth but long enough travel of the electrode in multiple small steps, is sturdy enough to prevent accidental movement of the electrode, easy to manipulate by the experimenter without interfering with the animal's behavior, small in size and light in weight.

span.label: microdrive
span.quote: Construction of the microdrive All drives are made from the same basic elements: a moving part, which carries the electrode and a fixed part, which is anchored to the skull.

span.label: probe depth in the brain (advanced daily by the microdrive screw)
span.term: probe depth in the brain (advanced daily by the microdrive screw)
span.quote: Lower the probe gradually by turning the screw by small increments (typically 1/8 to 1/4 turn per day, i.e. 35-70 micrometers) until the target structure is reached.

span.label: electrophysiological signals: local field potential and unit activity
span.term: electrophysiological signals: local field potential and unit activity
span.quote: Electrophysiological signals (local field potential and unit activity) vary depending on the recorded structure and the current behavior of the animal.

span.label: 20 000 Hz — wideband sampling rate of the chronic recordings, chosen so that both LFP oscillations and spikes can be studied
span.quote: Recordings are wideband and sampled at 20 000 Hz, which allows to study both local field potential oscillations (e.g. "theta" band 8 Hz rhythm) and neuronal spiking activity.

span.label: 35-70 micrometers — how far the probe is advanced per day (1/8 to 1/4 turn of the drive screw) while searching for the target structure
span.quote: Lower the probe gradually by turning the screw by small increments (typically 1/8 to 1/4 turn per day, i.e. 35-70 micrometers) until the target structure is reached.

span.label: 64 to 128 — number of sites now routinely recorded simultaneously in a behaving rodent, versus 2 sites with wire electrodes a decade earlier
span.quote: Today, it is as easy to record from 64 to 128 sites simultaneously in a behaving rodent as from 2 sites with wire electrodes just a decade ago.

span.label: 8 Hz — frequency of the theta-band local field potential oscillation seen in CA1 during open-field exploration
span.quote: Note the prominent 8 Hz (theta band) oscillation of the local field potential during exploration with superimposed spiking on multiple shanks and sites

span.label: 4-shank, 32-site — the probe configuration demonstrated
span.quote: Here, we describe the implantation of a 4-shank, 32-site probe attached to flexible polyimide cable, and mounted on a movable microdrive.

span.label: 20 000 Hz — the sampling rate allowing both field potentials and spikes from the same wideband signal
span.quote: Recordings are wideband and sampled at 20 000 Hz, which allows to study both local field potential oscillations (e.g. "theta" band 8 Hz rhythm) and neuronal spiking activity.

span.label: 64 to 128 sites — what is routine now against two sites a decade before
span.quote: Today, it is as easy to record from 64 to 128 sites simultaneously in a behaving rodent as from 2 sites with wire electrodes just a decade ago.

span.label: 8 Hz — the theta rhythm visible in the example hippocampal recording
span.quote: Note the prominent 8 Hz (theta band) oscillation of the local field potential during exploration with superimposed spiking on multiple shanks and sites (examples of spikes indicated by arrowheads).
